title: Maintenance routine - Wood cabinets
notes: Every month - Apply a wood protection product designed for wood cabinets.

title: Maintenance routine - Furnace / Air conditioning
notes: Every six months - Inspect filters for dust. Clean and replace filters. 20”x25”x4”

title: Maintenance routine - Plumbing
notes: Every month - Check under kitchen and bathroom cabinets for leaks. Tighten fittings carefully. Check the area around the hot water heater for leaks. Discoloration or blistering of the walls, ceilings, or floor coverings may indicate a leak.

title: Maintenance routine - Kitchen exhaust fan
notes: Every month - Remove and clean the filter. Clean accumulated grease deposits from the fan housing.

title: Maintenance routine - Faucet aerators
notes: Every month - Check for proper flow of water. If the flow is reduced, clean the aerator screens. During the first two months, the faucet aerators could require more frequent cleaning.

title: Maintenance routine - Perimeter inspection
notes: Every month - Look for evidence of termites on or near your foundation. If evidence of termites is found, please consult the termite section of this manual. Inspect landscaping and swales for proper drainage away from the home.

title: Maintenance routine - Exterior doors
notes: Every two months - Oil hinges and locks if required. Inspect finish for cracks and peeling. Use touchup paint or varnish where required.

title: Maintenance routine - Interior doors
notes: Every three months - Lubricate hinges.

title: Maintenance routine - Garage door
notes: Every three months - Lubricate hardware. Inspect mechanism for free travel. Adjust if necessary.

title: Maintenance routine - Tiled Areas
notes: Every three months - Inspect caulked areas for missing or damaged caulking. Re-caulkifnecessary.

title: Maintenance routine - Shower Doors
notes: Every three months - Inspect for proper fit. Adjust if necessary. Inspect caulking and re-caulk if necessary.

title: Maintenance Routine - Tub Enclosures
notes: Every three months - Inspect for proper fit. Adjust if necessary. Inspect caulking and re-caulk if necessary.

title: Maintenance routine - Air Conditioning System Condensation Line
notes: Every six months - Pour one (1) cup of water down the condensation line to flush the line.

title: Maintenance routine - Kitchen Tile Grout
notes: Every six months - Inspect for loose or missing grout. Re-grout if necessary. Recaulk at the edge of the backsplash if necessary.

title: Maintenance routine - Front Doors
notes: Every six months - Repaint or refinish if necessary. Consult your Homeowners' or Neighborhood Association regulations before your change the exterior paint color of your doors.

title: Maintenance routine - Gutters
notes: Every six months - Clean debris from gutters every six months and after storms.

title: Maintenance Routine - Exterior Paint
notes: Every year - Inspect for cracked and peeling paint and caulking. It is especially important to maintain the caulking around doors and windows. Repair and repaint if necessary. Consult your Homeowners' or Neighborhood Association regulations (if any) before you change the exterior paint colors. Southern and western exposures are especially subject to peeling and cracking. Inspect these areas twice each year. Caulk and repaint as necessary. French and wood doors should be repainted annually.

title: Maintenance routine - roof
notes: Every year - Inspect for damaged shingles or accumulated debris after storms and high winds. An annual inspection by a roofing professional is recommended. You may contact our Customer Service Department for the name and telephone number of your original roofing contractor.

title: Maintenance routine - Fireplace
notes: Every year - Have the chimney inspected annually. Cleaning by a professional chimney cleaner is recommended. Check to see that the damper opens properly and closes tightly. Inspect the chimney cap for blockages caused by birds or insects.

title: Maintenance routine - HVAC system
notes: Every year - We recommend an inspection by a heating professional every year. We also recommend using the original contractor for the life of the system.
